speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are here with a limp and localized pain, but no fever or acute distress. To begin, can you tell me exactly where it hurts and what activity was happening when you first noticed the limp?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the left knee pain favoring the left leg in a 7-year-old is concerning for a slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) or a fracture, even though he reports no trauma. To confirm this, I need to examine his hips, so please lift your shirt for me to inspect both knees and hips. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_Anteroposterior.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That confirms the pain is isolated to the left knee without systemic signs. To differentiate between a slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) and a tibial tubercle apophysitis, I need to check for tenderness specifically over the tibial tubercle and observe hip range of motion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE) is the primary concern given the 7-year-old age and limp, though Osgood-Schlatter disease remains a differential; imaging will confirm.
